meaning: Lines 126-127 set the wall flow two ways at once: it equals minus the rate of change of vessel volume, and minus compliance times the rate of change of transmural pressure. Together they pin V to Ptm through a constant compliance C, so the vessel wall obeys a linear pressure-volume law with no independent volume state.

could_move.what: Vessel volume V, and hence area A = V/(N_v*l_v), is tied to Ptm by constant C; any pressure-volume nonlinearity shows up as fit residual instead.
Resistance evolution is driven by V and D(V), so the linear-compliance assumption propagates into R and into the pressure drop.
The m5-vs-m6 comparison may partly measure this wall law rather than the intended model difference.
Two equations for ext.q plus D(V) and D(R) change the DAE structure MTK simplifies, so which variables remain states can shift.

expectation: Unknown in size. A constant C makes the wall stiffer or softer than a nonlinear law would be, most visibly where Ptm swings largest, i.e. during jugular compression. I cannot tell from this context whether the fit absorbs that into C and R.

check.why: Single-model entry point from the reach trace. One solve shows whether the two ext.q equations still simplify and integrate, and gives V and Ptm traces to inspect, without re-fitting both models in the deck.
